content: It's unclear whether addition or subtraction comes before or after division.
You said to round after division, but your solutions are not rounded.

I think you might want to change the variable name of [[i]] because it gets used in the for loop as well.

Also, the goal should probably say '<<add>> the index value to [[sum]].' instead of 'from'.
Is it supposed to say 'if a letter has an even index' or is it referring to the [[i]] variable index?

Working on that rn, trying to fix all the issues Sflubaduba, User123, and 5DN1L pointed out

[Goal]

- Please fix the add statement and the variable name "i", as suggested by @Sflubaduba.

- As @Sflubaduba has pointed out, the term "index" here is overloaded. You state that "If a number has an even index, add the index value from sum" but you solution only checks the 0-indexed index value of a letter (not the [[i]]-indexed index value your clash introduces). This creates some discrepancies in the clash; e.g. in the "Praise" test case, where using the [[i]]-indexed index values yields an answer of -603 instead of 603.

- Another thing I noticed in your solution: you divide sum by 2 on *each* iteration once all letters have been seen. This means that it is possible that division by 2 happens more than once, as seen in some of your cases. This is somewhat stated in your problem description "every time all the letters of the alphabet have been called" but this statement is unclear and can have multiple interpretations. It is better to make this rule explicit; one suggestion is to use bullet points to highlight that this rule is executed per letter seen.

[Constraints]

- Please move the last constraint to the Goal section.

- The test/validator case "Are we playing UNO?" violates the constraint 0 < n < 75. Please fix the case or update your constraints accordingly.

- It might be a good idea to limit the number of floating-point divisions required per test case.

[Cases]

- Please add more cases where [[i]] is more varied. There are too many cases where [[i]] is a small number like 0 or 1.

Thank you.

Just to add to @Sflubaduba's first comment,

* "[[i]] gets used in the for loop as well" refers to the variable name used in the for loop in the default code generated by the stub. That's why [[i]] should be changed to a different variable name so that it isn't overwritten. This is particularly important for players who want to use the default code without making significant changes to it.

* Both instances of "If a number" should be changed to "If a letter". "A" to "Z" are letters, not numbers.

As mentioned by both @Sflubaduba and @User123, the statement is confusing because it doesn't clearly distinguish between the indexes being used:

* deciding the operation (add or subtract) depends on the letter's 0-based index, whereas
* the index value actually being added or subtracted is the "i-based" index.

In addition to the excellent points already raised by @Sflubaduba and @User123, please also follow up on the following:

Goal
* [[sum]] is used but undefined. Please specify that its initial value is 0.

* Please change "[[i]] indexed" to "indexed starting at [[i]]" for clarity.

* Please specify that letter input should be treated in a case-insensitive manner.

Output
* Please specify that if the answer is an integer, it should be output without any decimal places; otherwise, it should be output with all decimal places and no trailing zeros.

Stub generator
* Please add a write statement, e.g. write answer.

Cases
* The uppercase letters K and W aren't used in any validators. Please modify the validators so that these letters are used in at least one validator.

* Please revise Validators 2 to 5 so that the input letters are more similar to those in their corresponding tests. For example, Test 2 uses a number of different lowercase letters, whereas Validator 2 uses only a few uppercase letters, so they aren't closely aligned.

* Please revise the cases so that each validator expects a similar *type* of output to its corresponding test, while the answers are still different. For example, both could expect small positive integers, or both could expect large negative floating-point values with three decimal places.

* There don't seem to be any clear patterns in the case progression. Please order the case pairs according to some meaningful criteria, or rename the cases to describe clearly their intended coverage.

Thanks.
I fixed everything- let me know if this all seems right.

It's a lot better. Just me being pedantic but there's a few things that I would change.

[Goal]
- if the value is even: add *to* total. if the value is odd: subtract *from*

- specify the rounding method (round half away from zero)

- "This applies once for a set of letters, and then only a new set of letters can enable another WILDCARD." People might overthink what constitutes a 'set' of letters. I think this phrasing would help: "Once a wildcard has been activated, only the letters that follow count towards the next wildcard."

- Maybe make it clear in the wildcard example that the letters do not need to appear in alphabetical order. Adding a random letter after B would suffice.

[Cases]
- It seems that all of the test cases have either all upper or all lower case while the validators tend to mix them. Include a test case with both upper and lower case (if I'm not mistaken. Apologies if I am)

- The answer is the same for each case pair, making it easier to hardcode. I know it's a bit harder to avoid that for this puzzle while ensuring that the pairs test the same situation, but I think it can be done. Maybe just change the value of [[v]] for every validator except the first.

In addition to what @Sflubaduba has mentioned:

Goal
* Please specify in a paragraph immediately after the first sentence in this section (not the Constraints section) that [[total]]'s initial value is {{0}}. (Also note that there's currently a typo in the constraint: "intitial".)

* Please change "even v-based value" to "even value".

* Please change "odd v-value" to "odd value".

* Please specify that letter input should be treated in a case-insensitive manner, rather than simply stating that the letters may or may not be capitalized, since the latter does not explain exactly how the input should be handled.

* Please change "round to the ones' place after division" to "round to the nearest integer. If the result is exactly halfway between two integers, round away from zero."

* Please change "called" to "encountered".

* Please change "ex." to "Example".

Constraints
* Please remove the third constraint.

Stub generator
* Please change "write sum" to "write total" for consistency.

Cases
* As for how to achieve case similarity, the key is usually to be similar in quantitative aspects and to be the same in qualitative aspects in each test / validator pair, in as many aspects as possible. Specifically,

  • n, v, total (quantitative): The magnitudes should be similar, but they need not be the same; in fact, it's preferable for them to differ slightly.

  • total when a WILDCARD is present (qualitative): The intermediate values before division by 2 should have the same characteristics: both should involve positive odd integers, positive even integers, negative odd integers, negative even integers, and/or zero.

  • letters (qualitative): The same letter cases should be used: either only lowercase, only uppercase, or a mix. Likewise, either both should contain a WILDCARD or neither should.

  • Number of WILDCARD occurrences (quantitative): The same number of WILDCARD occurrences (1, 2, or perhaps more if possible) should be present.

* It isn't necessary for Test 1 and Validator 1 to expect the same output.

* All letters in uppercase should be covered in at least one test and at least one validator.

* All letters in lowercase should be covered in at least one test and at least one validator.

Thanks.

Cases
* The scenario in which [[total]] is a positive even integer when a WILDCARD set is completed isn't covered by any cases. Therefore, please revise the final two cases as follows:

  • Triple Wildcard Threat (Test 6)
    - Change n to 110.
    - Add "hi" at the beginning.
    - Add "END" before "dwarf" near the end.

  • Three-Wildcard Validator (Validator 6)
    - Change n to 107.
    - Change v to 79.
    - Add "oh" at the beginning.

Constraints
* Please change 105 to 200 to accommodate the above revisions.

Thanks.
